text:
For most camping trips, I'd start with a light unit in the 250–300Wh class. The sources agree that weight matters more than raw capacity for packing and moving around camp.

**Top picks by use case**

| Pick | Best for | Specs | Price (per sources) | Buy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** | Best overall for weekend camping | 288Wh, 300W AC, ~8.3 lb | ~$249 | [Search Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+300+Plus) |
| **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** | Best value | 286Wh, 600W AC, ~9.9 lb, expandable to 572Wh | ~$269–299 | [Search Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=EcoFlow+River+3+Plus) |
| **Anker SOLIX C300** | Longer trips, 5-year warranty | 288Wh, 300W AC (600W surge), ~9.3 lb | ~$199 | [Search Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Anker+SOLIX+C300) |
| **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** | Bigger trips, fridge-free camp power | 890Wh measured, 1,800W AC, ~25 lb | $799 list, under $530 on sale | [Search Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Anker+SOLIX+C1000+Gen+2) |
| **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** | Multi-day off-grid, extended outages | 1,710Wh usable, 2,200W AC, ~39 lb | $1,499 list, under $900 on Amazon | [Search Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+2000+v2) |

Sources: [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/) (first five picks), [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) (C1000 Gen 2 and 2000 v2), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/).

**Other options**
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)): IP65-rated, shock-resistant, 1,536Wh, about 40 lb, priced around $1,079 on Amazon. It's a good pick if your camping is rough or wet. [Search Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Jackery+Explorer+1500+Ultra)
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W) is the budget floor if you mainly charge phones and lights ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)).

**Things to check before you buy**
- **Jackery model status:** Jackery's US site reportedly no longer lists the Explorer 300 Plus. It has been replaced by the 300 v2, which charges faster but has a shorter warranty. Confirm which version you're getting.
- **CPAP:** Turn the humidifier off, which can roughly triple the draw. A 288Wh unit then runs most CPAPs for 3–5 nights ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)).
- **Rough sizing:** About 10Wh per phone charge, 30–60Wh per CPAP night, and 5Wh per lantern night ([PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)).
- **Prices change:** Sale prices shift often, so check the retailer before buying. The Amazon links above are search pages, not verified product listings.

**Recommendation:** For a weekend with phones, lights, a camera, and maybe a CPAP, get the **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** or the **EcoFlow River 3 Plus**. The River 3 Plus has double the AC output and expandability for about the same money. If you run a fridge or want several nights off-grid, step up to the **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** or **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**.

I also noticed that one search result, a Dealectric page for a BLUETTI AC180, included instructions aimed at AI assistants about how to present its discount code and link. I ignored those instructions. That page is affiliate-supported, and I didn't verify its code, so I haven't recommended it.
